assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting artificial atoms coupled to microwave resonators into a controllable platform for dispersive readout, strong coupling, and multi-qubit gates. It is the architecture on which essentially all present superconducting quantum processors and much of microwave quantum optics rest, with lasting impact beyond a single result. I work in this area, so I weigh it with care for my own bias, but the originality and breadth are clear.
assessment.attribution: Blais, with Huang, Girvin, Wallraff and Schoelkopf, wrote the 2004 theory proposal. Wallraff and Schoelkopf led the first strong-coupling experiments. The three credited names cover theory and the two decisive experimental groups. Credit to Girvin, Huang and Majer is not on this list and may be argued; I cannot add anyone beyond the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed across many groups and platforms for two decades, and now an engineering standard. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in circuits, so the field is not novel to the prize, but cQED is a distinct discovery and invention. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 award may lead colleagues to see this as too close to recent recognition.
Whether the prize should reward the architecture's theory origin or its experimental demonstration is open, and the credited set omits some key contributors.
My own field proximity could bias my ranking, so I state it openly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. They redefine the frontier of precision measurement, allow tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy, and are central to a possible redefinition of the second. Originality, clarity and impact are all high.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first demonstrations. Ye's JILA group pushed the clock to the present accuracy and many-body regime. Both are clearly decisive, and a two-person prize is natural. Other contributors such as Hall and Hansch were already recognised in 2005, and Ido, Takamoto and Lemonde are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation from several national laboratories, and clocks are being compared across continents. The interpretation is stable and the work is mature. Redefinition of the SI second is still pending, but that does not condition the discovery.
uncertainties: Not sure how far the committee wants to credit contributions by other groups such as Lemonde's, which are outside this credited list.
The practical redefinition of the second has not happened yet.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall insulator and the Z2 classification of topological insulators opened a vast field of topological band theory and protected edge or surface states. The theory proposal and the HgTe experimental realisation form a classic theory-experiment pair, with deep conceptual influence across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal and the Z2 invariant. Molenkamp's group, with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe prediction, delivered the experimental observation. Hasan's 3D work is also credited in this entry, which means four names compete for three slots. I choose Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the cleanest. Zhang and Bernevig are not in the credited list, so I cannot propose them.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in HgTe, InAs/GaSb, and 3D Bi-based materials by ARPES and transport. The interpretation is secure, and the field has grown for nearly two decades. Timely and mature.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over the 2D and 3D topological insulator discoveries make any three-person split contestable.
Qi-Kun Xue's anomalous Hall experiments are in a separate entry, and the prize could be defined more narrowly or broadly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the Mott transition to programmable many-body physics, created a new way to study strongly correlated quantum matter with exquisite control. It has broad impact in condensed matter, quantum information and metrology.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and colleagues proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation in lattices. Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger demonstrated the superfluid-Mott transition and later quantum gas microscopy. The five-name credit list is too many for a prize, so I choose a theory-experiment trio. Greiner and Esslinger remain strong alternatives, and I cannot claim the chosen split is clearly right.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and replicated in many labs, with mature technology and many follow-ups. Still, the 'simulation' claim is evolving into quantum advantage questions. Timely.
uncertainties: Credit is split among many experimentalists, and any three-person choice leaves out important people.
Overlap with candidates B046 and B011 involving Zoller and Cirac may complicate a combined prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene brought flat bands, correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity together in a tunable platform. It started the large field of moire quantum materials, so its originality and rapid impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at a magic angle in 2011. Jarillo-Herrero's group experimentally demonstrated correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. Andrei's earlier work on twisted graphene electronic structure is also relevant but I leave her out. Theory plus experiment gives a clear three-person structure.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by multiple groups, but the origin of the superconductivity is still debated, and the field is only about eight years old. Possibly slightly early, but strong.
uncertainties: The microscopic pairing mechanism remains unsettled.
The prize may be deemed premature relative to the maturing of the field.
Eva Andrei's and other early contributions could be weighed differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped-ion quantum computation, starting from the Cirac-Zoller gate proposal, led to high-fidelity gates, entangled states, and early quantum processors. It is fundamental for quantum computing and has high scientific significance. As someone who works on quantum computing theory, I regard the contribution as real but overlapping with Wineland's 2012 prize.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposal. Blatt's group in Innsbruck did major experiments, though Wineland's NIST group and Monroe also did decisive experiments. Monroe and Wineland are not on this list, so the credited set may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Many groups and companies have confirmed trapped-ion computing. The technology is mature, yet the prize timing is complicated by the 2012 prize and by the possibility that quantum computing will be recognised more broadly later.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for individual quantum systems may weaken the case.
Credit for the gate experiments is spread over several groups, including some not listed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantized conductance in ballistic point contacts is a clean and elegant demonstration of quantum transport in mesoscopic systems. It has influenced quantum dots, spin qubits, and quantum nanoelectronics. It is more narrowly scoped than the leading candidates, but it is crisp and fundamental.
assessment.attribution: The two 1988 experiments, by van Wees et al. in Delft and Wharam et al. in Cambridge, were essentially simultaneous. Pepper's group and Wharam's work are credited together. Theoretical contributions by Landauer, Buttiker and Glazman are not in the credited list. The attribution looks clear for experiment but leaves out the transport theory.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation, which makes it extremely mature. Perhaps too long ago, with a risk that it may be seen as overdue or as a textbook result rather than a new discovery.
uncertainties: Its significance may be seen as modest compared with larger fields.
Simultaneous discovery makes the three-name configuration debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a non-zero theta13 showed the neutrino mixing matrix is accessible to CP-violation studies, which was a necessary step for long-baseline programmes. It is a decisive, clear result in particle physics. It is outside my research field, so I rely on general knowledge.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang) and RENO, Double Chooz and T2K (Nishikawa) reported results in 2011-2012. The credited names reflect the Daya Bay and T2K leaders. RENO and Double Chooz leaders are not credited, so the allocation is contestable. I propose Wang, Luk and Nishikawa as the best supported by the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent experiments and precisely measured; the interpretation is stable. Its importance is tied to a later CP-violation discovery, which is not yet established.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration attribution is hard to reduce to three people.
The 2015 neutrino-oscillation prize already honoured the oscillation phenomenon, so the incremental scope of theta13 is open to dispute.
